svg.title: Cervical screening: who is screened and how the sample is taken, then the primary HPV test result decides the next step: HPV negative returns in 5 years, HPV 16/18 goes to colposcopy, other high-risk HPV is triaged by reflex cytology; the HPV vaccine prevents but does not replace screening

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Cervical screening: the PRIMARY HPV TEST result decides the next step

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: WHO: any ASYMPTOMATIC person with a cervix who has EVER been sexually active, from ≈ AGE 25

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: SAMPLE: provider-collected (speculum + broom/brush) OR self-collected vaginal swab

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: test for high-risk HPV FIRST · cytology (LBC) only triages a positive · inadequate sample → repeat

svg.text: SCREEN: the HPV result picks the branch

svg.text: HPV is the cause: test for it directly · 16/18 carry the highest cancer risk
